residence-procedure.title: Local-residence requirement disclosure
residence-procedure.summary: A college/campus/program may require up to 24 major credits locally. Specific courses cannot be mandated except a required senior seminar or capstone. Such requirements must appear in the academic plan, Bulletin major description and college/department graduation materials; advising must address them. Students can raise noncompliance with the undergraduate associate dean.

transfer-completion-procedure.title: Transfer review and graduation-document deadline
transfer-completion-procedure.summary: Before taking outside courses, use the transfer-credit tool and consult an adviser about transferability and degree applicability. Unevaluated courses require a current syllabus and formal review. Official credit documents must reach Admissions at least 30 days before the graduating semester’s last class day; college approval is required for deadline exceptions.

general-education-policy.title: General education distribution, breadth and overlap
general-education-policy.summary: The 45-credit GE allocation is 15 foundations (9 writing/speaking, 6 quantification), 15 breadth (3 in each of five domains), 6 integrative studies and 9 exploration. Foundations require C and cannot be inter-domain; breadth also excludes inter-domain. Exploration requires 3 natural-science credits plus 6 from permitted domains, including limited advanced language. Breadth/exploration cannot use the major’s own department/program or its cross-listed courses; integrative studies is exempt. Published flexibility permits appropriate 200–499 substitutions and qualifying language beyond degree minima. Program-identified major overlap is limited by the domain caps; integrative-study courses cannot enter that overlap statement.

ist-major-guidance.title: College major-entry and focus guidance
ist-major-guidance.summary: The college requires a 2.00 entrance GPA and C grades in MATH140, the stated programming sequences, DS200 or STAT200, and A-I100. Choose a series within one application focus; the college directs the actual course lists to the Bulletin. Academic plans depend on entry semester, and prerequisite flowcharts are planning aids alongside official degree checks.

ist-faq-exemption.title: College internship exception and transfer-admission scope
ist-faq-exemption.summary: AIMA is expressly exempt from the general IST undergraduate internship graduation requirement. The FAQ currently says University Park IST undergraduate programs do not accept external transfer students and reassess this policy annually; this admissions rule is distinct from evaluation of outside credits for enrolled students. The general focus-choice FAQ does not override the AIMA-specific requirement to use its published focus areas.

engineering-department-guidance.title: Department supporting-list boundary
engineering-department-guidance.summary: The department confirms 27 approved technical-elective credits, including 15 at the 400 level, plus 3 approved nontechnical credits and a one-credit seminar. This public page does not enumerate or link the approved lists. Its condensed additional-course presentation is not used to replace the Bulletin’s separate programming sequences and speech alternatives.
